lastCompletedStory.title: Drop bun-version-conditioned skips; make Ink stdin tests version-agnostic

openQuestions: The story's notes assumed the root cause was purely bun-version macrotask scheduling (patterns.md CAM-186 bullet: '2 ticks on 1.2.x, 1 tick on >=1.3') and prescribed 'flushing enough macrotask ticks (two)'. Empirically that prescription was insufficient and flaky: repeated full-`bun test`-suite runs (30+ trials) showed a fixed 2-tick wait failing roughly 1 run in 4-8 under full-suite CPU contention, and even a fixed larger count (4 ticks, or a 3000ms bounded poll) still occasionally missed. Root-caused it instead to `ink-testing-library`'s fake Stdout having no `rows` getter, which makes Ink's `getWindowSize` shell out to `tput` synchronously via the `terminal-size` package on EVERY render; under concurrent-suite load that spawn can take up to several seconds. Fix implemented in `test/helpers/mock-terminal-size.ts` (installTerminalSizeMock, uses `mock.module('terminal-size', ...)` to stub it out entirely) rather than the tick-count approach the story notes suggested. `test/helpers/flush-ink.ts`'s `flushInk` (two ticks) and `waitForFrame` (content-based bounded poll, default 3000ms) are kept as defense-in-depth on top of the mock, not as the primary fix.

Verified via WebSearch (Step 5.5) that `mock.module()` is documented to override already-imported modules via live bindings (bun.sh/docs/test/mocks), and that `mock.restore()` has a known upstream issue (oven-sh/bun#7823) of NOT reverting a `mock.module()` call -- this matches what empirical testing in this session found (mock.restore() did not undo a terminal-size module mock). Because of this, `installTerminalSizeMock()` is intentionally process-global and idempotent (a guard flag, not a restore/undo path); it will silently also speed up/stabilize ANY other ink-testing-library-based test file that runs in the same `bun test` process after ours, which is a strict improvement (removes a synchronous subprocess spawn) but is worth knowing about if a future story ever needs to assert something about REAL terminal dimensions in an ink-testing-library render (none currently do).

US-005 (guard gate forbidding toolchain-version-conditioned skips) and US-006/US-007 remain queued next, continuing the toolchain-parity thread from US-001..US-003 (see prior handoff `nextStoryContext` for the established seams: `src/config/toolchain.ts`'s readPinnedBunVersion/readPinnedNodeVersion, `buildDockerBuildArgv`'s resolveBunVersion/resolveNodeVersion). US-005's guard should probably grep for the SAME anti-pattern this story just removed (`Bun.version` / `process.version` conditioned `skipIf`/`test.skip`), not just the literal `bunVersionOk` identifier name, since a differently-named future probe would otherwise slip through a name-only grep.
nextStoryContext: US-005 (Add check:all guard gate forbidding toolchain-version-conditioned skips) is next by priority. It should add a new gate function to scripts/check-all.ts's GATES manifest (see patterns.md 'Gate-spine convention' bullet) that greps test/ for Bun.version/process.version-conditioned skip patterns and fails if any are found, now that US-004 has cleared the only two pre-existing instances. Read patterns.md's new CAM-201 bullet (this story) for why the fix approach shifted from tick-counting to mocking terminal-size; that context is unrelated to US-005's own scope but explains why test/dashboard.test.ts and test/ui/init-setup-screen-keys.test.ts look different from what the original story notes described.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed via WebSearch (direct WebFetch to bun.sh failed with no output in this sandbox, so WebSearch was used as the fallback path): mock.module() overrides a module even if already imported (live ESM bindings), and mock.restore() has a known upstream issue (oven-sh/bun#7823) of not reverting a mock.module() call. Both match this session's empirical findings exactly (installTerminalSizeMock() installed after ink-testing-library/ink already imported terminal-size still took effect; a manual mock.restore() probe did not undo the mock), so the implementation's process-global idempotent-installer design (no restore/undo path attempted) is the correct approach given the documented and known-buggy restore behavior, not a workaround for a misunderstood API.
